text:
marta: Canary nodes showing big memory spike after today's runtime merge — ~1.6GB steady growth on longctx runs. Anyone else seeing this?

ci-bot: [ALERT] canary-03 memory-usage > 85% for 5m. Link: https://ci/redwood/canary/3400000123

sam: saw an OOM on test16 around 10:22. stack trace points at cache allocation path.

jia: I'm pulling a heap profile now. initial glance: key-value cache allocations jumped, fragmentation up. dumping top hot paths.

jia: ```
# heap profile summary
total: 3.1GB
key-value-cache: 1.9GB (+1.4GB vs baseline)
batching-router: 0.35GB
kernel-selection: 0.2GB
``` 

andre: that matches my repro. The kernel-router merge (commit abcd1234) changed steering rules to prefer 'wide' kernels at seq len 512-2048.

marta: so the kernel choice increased per-request scratch allocation? or we warmed new cache shards?

sam: seems both. Wider kernels allocate larger temporary buffers and we ended up striping cache slabs differently; more small-fragment allocations.

jia: I ran a bisect between abcd1234 and previous commit. Confirmed regression introduced by abcd1234. Bisect notes: https://git/repo/commit/abcd1234

andre: quick thought — revert steering change or narrow the heuristic to avoid wide-kernel preference for longctx heavy workloads.

sam: repro command I used:

```
./run_infer --model rdl-3 --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --profile-heap > heap.log
```

marta: CI is also showing perf/cpu-throughput flake after same merge. Might be related.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Revert PR pr/1102 created by marta to revert kernel-router steering. Tests queued.

marta: I've requested expedited rollback. If tests pass, we'll revert canary at 10:50.

andre: long-term fix: add a cost model that includes scratch buffer size + slab fragmentation penalty. For now revert.

sam: after reverting locally memory returns to baseline. I'll push CI run to verify with longctx stress.

ci-bot: [SUCCESS] pr/1102 tests passed in 7m. staging deploy ok.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Revert pr/1102 promoted to canary. Monitoring CPU/memory for 30m.

marta: thanks y'all. followups: add regression test for cache-frag with seq=1024 and a perf eval for kernel steering.

jia: I'll open issue with traces and attach heap dumps. Tagging @eng-sre for monitoring thresholds.

sam: note to self: watch for creeping fragmentation metric 'cache.frag_ratio' over next 24h :eyes:

ops-bot: Monitoring: no further OOMs in canary after revert (10m window). Will update channel with 1h and 24h summaries.
